pl-l4d18c6-d1e115.summary: States that God did not give priests the power to cleanse and remit eternal death, but gave them the power of binding and loosing, that is, of showing people bound or loosed. So the Lord first healed the leper himself, then sent him to the priests to be shown clean, and gave Lazarus, already alive, to the disciples to unbind; though one is loosed before God, he is not held loosed in the Church's sight except by the priest's judgment. The evangelical priest works in loosing and retaining sins as the legal priest did with lepers, leprosy figuring sin.
claims: Priests show people bound or loosed.
The priest's judgment makes loosing manifest in the Church.

pl-l4d18c6-d1e118.summary: Quotes Jerome on 'I will give you the keys': some, not understanding this, take on Pharisaic arrogance, thinking they condemn the innocent or loose the guilty, though before God not the priest's sentence but the guilty person's life is weighed. In Leviticus lepers show themselves to priests, who do not make them leprous or clean but discern who is clean or unclean; so here.
claims: Priests do not make people guilty or innocent but discern them.

pl-l4d18c6-d1e133.summary: Draws out that God does not follow the Church's judgment, which sometimes judges by deception or ignorance, but always judges by truth. Evangelical priests have the same right and office in remitting and retaining sins as the legal priests had with lepers: they forgive or retain sins when they judge and show them forgiven or retained by God, as priests put God's name on Israel but he blesses.
claims: God judges by truth, not by the Church's possibly mistaken judgment.
Priests forgive by declaring God's forgiveness.

pl-l4d18c6-d1e143.summary: Adds that priests also bind when they impose penitential satisfaction on those who confess, and loose when they remit some of it or admit those purged by it to the sacraments, as Leo noted; in this way too priests are said to forgive or retain sins, exercising justice by binding with just penalty and mercy by relaxing it or reconciling.
claims: Priests bind by imposing satisfaction and loose by remitting it or readmitting to communion.

pl-l4d18c6-d1e152.summary: Notes that those bound by penitential satisfaction are thereby shown loosed from sins, since satisfaction is imposed only on one the priest judges truly penitent; to others he does not impose it, and thereby shows the sin retained by God.
claims: Imposing satisfaction declares the penitent loosed.

pl-l4d18c6-d1e155.summary: Cites Augustine to show this pertains to the keys: one who does penance without the priest's judgment frustrates the Church's keys, if pardon is obtained without oral confession of the crime.
claims: Penance without the priest frustrates the keys.

pl-l4d18c6-d1e164.summary: Describes another mode of binding and loosing, by excommunication: when someone, called three times by canonical discipline to amend a manifest crime and scorning satisfaction, is cut off by the Church's sentence from the place of prayer, the sacraments, and the fellowship of the faithful, so that, ashamed, he may repent and be saved; if he repents, he is readmitted and reconciled. This anathema inflicts on those justly struck the withdrawal of God's grace and protection, leaving them to themselves and giving the devil more power over them; the Church's prayers and blessings do not help them.
claims: Excommunication cuts off from the sacraments and the faithful.
The justly excommunicated lose grace, protection, and the Church's prayers.

pl-l4d18c6.summary: God did not give priests the power to cleanse the soul and remit eternal death, but the power of binding and loosing, that is, of showing people bound or loosed: as Christ healed the leper and then sent him to the priests, and gave Lazarus, already alive, to the disciples to unbind, one loosed before God is held loosed in the Church's sight only by the priest's judgment, as the legal priests judged lepers. Jerome: priests do not make people clean or unclean but discern them; God follows not the Church's judgment, which can err, but the truth. Priests also bind by imposing satisfaction and loose by remitting some of it or readmitting to communion; imposing satisfaction shows the penitent loosed. Augustine: whoever does penance without the priest's judgment frustrates the keys. Another mode of binding and loosing is excommunication, by which one refusing to amend a public crime after three warnings is cut off from the sacraments and the faithful, losing grace, protection, and the Church's prayers, until he repents and is reconciled.
claims: Priests bind and loose by declaring people bound or loosed.
God follows the truth, not the Church's judgment, which can err.
Priests bind by imposing satisfaction and loose by remitting it or readmitting to communion.
Penance without the priest's judgment frustrates the keys.
Excommunication is another mode of binding, withdrawing grace and the Church's prayers.
